questions.stem: A ball is projected from level ground with speed $20\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ at $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, the maximum height reached is

options.whyWrong: Comes from $u^2\sin\theta/2g$: the sine was not squared.
Comes from $u^2\cos^2\theta/2g$: cos was used for the vertical component.
Comes from $u^2/2g$: the whole speed was treated as vertical.

questions.solution:
**Key idea:** only the vertical component $u\sin\theta$ decides the height.

1. $u_y = 20 \sin 30^\circ = 10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$
2. At the top $v_y = 0$, so $H = \dfrac{u_y^2}{2g} = \dfrac{100}{20}$
3. **$H = 5\ \text{m}$**
hints: Which component of the velocity decides how high the ball goes?
At the highest point the vertical velocity is zero. Use $v^2 = u^2 - 2gh$ vertically.

questions.stem: A stone is thrown from level ground with speed $20\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ at an angle of $15^\circ$ to the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, find its horizontal range in metres.
A particle is projected with speed $30\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ at $30^\circ$ above the horizontal from level ground ($g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$). Its time of flight is

options.whyWrong: This is only the time to the highest point.
Comes from $2u\cos\theta/g$: cos was used for the vertical component.
Comes from $2u/g$: the whole speed was treated as vertical.

questions.solution:
**Key idea:** the flight is symmetric, so total time = 2 × time to reach the top.

1. $u_y = 30 \sin 30^\circ = 15\ \text{m s}^{-1}$
2. Time to top $= u_y/g = 1.5\ \text{s}$
3. **$T = 3\ \text{s}$**
hints: Find the vertical component of velocity first.
